provider: Radicle Garden (hosted seed) + permissionless public seeds

free_tier.stated: 5 GB of storage to start with on a Garden subscription ('talk to us if you need more'); public permissionless seed nodes self-configure their own limit, e.g. 10 GB observed on a community node
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Served over HTTP from designated node subdomains (`node-name.radicle.garden`) without published egress metering. Peer-to-peer replication allows multiple network nodes to mirror repositories without centralized bandwidth charges.

tooling: `rad` CLI (Radicle heartwood), git remote `rad://`. Real client, actively developed.
chaining: Replication is the chaining primitive: each additional seed that follows your repo (rad id allow-list) is another free full copy and another serving endpoint. Content is addressed by git OID so it is verifiable. But it is a *replication* multiplier, not a capacity multiplier. Total bytes are still bounded by the largest seed.
limits_note: 5 GB on Garden (paid add-on beyond), per-account. Public permissive seeds are free but each sets its own cap. Fetching needs at least one node online holding the data.

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: Availability is the weak point, not durability: if no seed holds the repo, it is unreachable until a peer comes back. Garden states it is 'walkaway-safe'. Losing the host does not lose your local repo.
